text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read, understand, and maintain. For example, you might rename unclear variables, break a long function into smaller ones, or remove repeated code. Refactoring does not add new features or fix bugs; the program should behave exactly the same after the changes. It also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick solutions make code messy over time. Although refactoring takes extra effort, it saves time later and keeps projects healthy.
